strategy_objective_guidance:
- Single scored term: `combined_score = target_ratio * validity`, where `target_ratio = sum(radii)/2.635` and `validity ∈ {0,1}` is a hard gate. Effectively the objective is just the sum of 26 radii, all-or-nothing on validity.
- Validity constraints (tolerance 1e-6): no NaN, radii ≥ 0, every circle inside the unit square (x±r, y±r within [0,1]), and no pairwise overlap (dist ≥ r_i + r_j − 1e-6). Shapes must be exactly (26,2) and (26,).
- No reward for runtime (only a ~350 s hard timeout), determinism, elegance, or reported_sum accuracy (mismatch is only a warning). No partial credit for near-valid packings — an overlap of 1e-5 zeroes the entire score.
- The whole problem is one lever: maximize Σr subject to hard geometric constraints. There is no tradeoff between sub-scores; the only risk is validity failure. Scores above 1.0 are possible (target 2.635 is not a cap).
- Complete input is known in advance: the program receives nothing at runtime; n=26 and the unit square are fixed. This is a fully offline, deterministic construction problem — the constructor may embed a precomputed/painstakingly optimized layout, or run a long offline-style optimization *inside* the constructor (up to ~350 s) and emit the final centers/radii. Nothing forces a "pure explicit formula"; a constructor that internally runs batch optimization and then outputs explicit arrays is fully compliant and typically scores higher.
- Note the 1e-6 slack: solutions can be tightened to exactly touch constraints with a safety margin ~1e-7, and a common failure mode is optimizing right up to the tolerance and tripping it. Always re-validate inside the program and shrink/repair before returning.
strategy_diverge_guidance:
- Known-best layout transcription: hardcode the published best-known n=26 packing (centers/radii from packomania / Erich Friedman tables), scaled to the unit square; pure numpy constants. Mechanism: starts at or near score >1.0 with zero search cost. Verify with the same tolerance as the evaluator.
- Offline nonlinear optimization inside the constructor: treat centers and radii as 78 variables, maximize Σr with scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP or trust-constr) using constraint dicts for all 26·25/2 pairwise distances plus boundary constraints; scipy.optimize.minimize: method='SLSQP', method='trust-constr'. Mechanism: directly optimizes the scored quantity under the exact evaluator constraints; the 350 s budget permits a full solve at runtime.
- Multi-start stochastic search: random or lattice initializations followed by scipy.optimize.differential_evolution or scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on a penalized objective (Σr − λ·violations), then a final feasible projection. Mechanism: escapes the symmetric local optima that hexagonal hand layouts get stuck in.
- Structural constructor families (distinct geometries, not one family): (a) curved-chain / "s" arrangements of near-equal circles along the square's diagonal with corner fillers; (b) mixed-radius shell layout — one large central circle, rings of smaller circles, corner circles; (c) row/column lattice with alternating radii (large-small-large) tuned per row. Each gives a different parametric family whose few parameters (radii per row, offsets) can be optimized by scipy.optimize.minimize.
- LP/SOCP-style feasibility-and-growth iteration: iteratively solve for a common radius scale factor s such that scaled layout (s·r_i) is feasible, using scipy.optimize.brentq on the max-violation function; scipy.optimize: brentq, root. Mechanism: given any fixed contact topology, this finds the exact maximal uniform scaling — a cheap, reliable exploit of any good topology.
strategy_refine_guidance:
- Topology-preserving polish: freeze the contact graph (which circles touch which and which touch walls) and solve the resulting system of quadratic touch equations with scipy.optimize.fsolve / scipy.optimize.root (method='lm'); then verify all gaps ≥ 1e-7. Mechanism: the optimum of any packing is a jammed configuration — solving the exact tangency equations squeezes out the last 1e-3–1e-2 of radius sum.
- Per-circle radius growth loop: repeatedly pick the circle with the largest feasible growth headroom (distance to nearest constraint minus r_i) and grow it by that headroom minus 1e-7; re-solve positions with scipy.optimize.minimize after each growth round. Budget: run until total growth per round < 1e-9 or ~300 s elapsed.
- Perturb-and-repair refinement: random Gaussian perturbation of centers (σ ≈ 1e-3), re-solve feasibility with SLSQP (ftol=1e-12, maxiter=1000), accept if Σr increases and validate_packing-equivalent check passes with margin 5e-7. Mechanism: hill-climbing on the exact scored quantity with validity guaranteed by an internal replica of the evaluator's checks.
- Symmetry breaking: take a symmetric candidate, split it into left/right halves with independent radii, re-optimize; edge effects mean asymmetric packings often beat symmetric ones by ~1e-3.
- Safety-margin calibration: after optimization, compute min over all constraints of (slack), and uniformly shrink all radii by max(0, −min_slack) + 1e-7 so the evaluator's 1e-6 tolerance is never triggered; cost in score is ~2.6e-6, negligible versus a zeroed score.
- Warm-start portfolio: run 2–3 of the divergent families above in-process (each ~60–100 s with scipy.optimize), keep the best validated result, and hardcode the winning layout as a fallback constant so the program is robust to optimizer flakiness within the timeout.

strategies.title: [slsqp-multistart] Full 78-variable constrained optimization with deterministic
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: direct nonlinear constrained optimization of all centers+radii
Replacement scope: Replace `construct_packing`'s hexagonal layout generation and the entire `compute_max_radii` function with a single scipy SLSQP solve over 78 variables (26 x, 26 y, 26 r), objective −Σr, constraints: for each pair (i,j): (x_i−x_j)²+(y_i−y_j)² − (r_i+r_j)² ≥ 0; for each circle: x−r ≥ 0, y−r ≥ 0, 1−x−r ≥ 0, 1−y−r ≥ 0. Multistart from (a) the incumbent hex layout with radii 0.09, (b) a perturbed hex layout, (c) a jittered 5×5+1 grid. Keep the best validated result; fall back to the incumbent hex construction if SLSQP fails.
Compute budget: ≤3 starts × maxiter 300 SLSQP iterations, ftol 1e-12; expected evaluation time well under 60 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's greedy pairwise-scaling radii computation is provably suboptimal (it shrinks both circles of a touching pair even when only one is constrained, and never moves centers); joint optimization of positions and radii unlocks the gap between the current 1.587 and the known ~2.6 region. Expected-gain check: any SLSQP solution with Σr > 1.5869 strictly beats the incumbent's sum_radii; the hex seed with r=0.095 uniform is already feasible with Σr=2.47, so the optimizer starts above the incumbent's objective and can only improve it.

strategies.title: [greedy-growth] Topology-free greedy per-circle radius growth with position re-s
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: iterative growth loop (exploitation of a fixed layout)
Replacement scope: Replace `compute_max_radii` with a growth loop: initialize all radii to a small feasible value (e.g., 0.05) on the incumbent centers, then repeatedly (1) for each circle compute its headroom = min over walls and neighbors of (constraint distance − r_i), (2) grow the circle with the largest headroom by (headroom − 1e-7), (3) every ~10 growth steps re-run a short SLSQP position-only solve (52 variables, radii frozen) to let centers drift away from contacts. Terminate when per-round growth < 1e-9 or 200 s elapse.
Compute budget: growth loop unbounded iterations but capped by 200 s wall clock; position re-solves ≤ 20 × maxiter 200; expected total < 250 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's proportional pairwise scaling loses radius mass whenever a constrained circle is scaled down along with its neighbor; the greedy loop grows only the circle with slack, so total radius is monotonically non-decreasing and strictly increases whenever any circle has headroom. Expected-gain check: starting from the incumbent's radii (Σr = 1.5869), any circle with positive headroom yields strict increase; since the incumbent's greedy scaling leaves visible gaps in the dropped-circle corner region, headroom > 0 exists by construction, so Σr > 1.5869 is guaranteed after one round.

strategies.title: [diagonal-chain] Curved S-chain of near-equal circles along the diagonal with co
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: diagonal-chain-seed
Replacement scope: add `_chain_seed()` and insert it as the top-priority seed in `construct_packing()`'s `seeds` list; keep the incumbent hex/shell seeds and SLSQP `_run` machinery unchanged.
Compute budget: no new optimizer; one extra SLSQP start (maxiter 400) added to the existing ≤7-start loop, expected evaluation-time increase ≈ +2–3 s.
Gain mechanism: the incumbent's seeds are all hexagonal/ring lattices, whose equal-radius ceiling for 26 circles in a unit square is Σr ≈ 26·(1/(2·5))·(≈0.97) ≈ 2.52–2.58; the best-known packings for n≈25–30 in a square use a curved "S"-shaped chain of touching near-equal circles running corner-to-corner with smaller circles filling the two remaining corners. Construction: place 18 circles of radius r≈0.095 as a staggered chain following two arcs (centers on the curve y = 0.5 + 0.35·sin(π·(x−0.1)/0.8), sampled at arc-length spacing 2r·0.99), plus 4 corner circles of radius ≈0.065 at (r',r')-type positions, plus 4 edge-midpoint circles ≈0.08 — a genuinely different contact topology (chain-of-contacts rather than triangular lattice) that SLSQP then relaxes. Validity is preserved because every candidate still passes through the existing `_feasible` gate with the incumbent fallback retained.
Expected-gain check: the chain topology has a strictly larger uniform-radius bound (18·0.095 + 4·0.065 + 4·0.08 = 2.53 before relaxation, versus the hex seed's 26·0.0985 = 2.56 frozen lattice that SLSQP cannot leave), and after SLSQP relaxation of the chain's 78 free variables the local optimum is a different basin; the falsifiable threshold is combined_score > 0.977261 (Σr > 2.5751) on the evaluator.

strategies.title: [row-alternating] Per-row alternating large/small radius lattice with independen
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: row-alternating-lattice
Replacement scope: replace `_shell_seed()` (its mixed-ring layout plateaus) with `_row_seed()` producing the layout, and feed it as the primary seed in `construct_packing()`; keep `_hex_seed` as fallback.
Compute budget: Nelder–Mead on ≤5 structural parameters (row y-offsets, two radii values, per-row x-offset), ≤8 starts × maxiter 300, then the existing single SLSQP start from the result; expected total ≈ +4 s.
Gain mechanism: instead of one global radius, use rows of alternating radii: rows 1,3,5 hold 5 circles of radius a, rows 2,4 hold 4 circles of radius b>a placed in the gaps of adjacent rows (x-offset by half-spacing), plus 2 extra circles in the widest residual pockets; the degree of freedom the incumbent lacks is that small circles in row gaps let the large circles be larger than the uniform hex limit — the per-row spacing for radius-a circles can exceed 2a because the b-circles occupy the interstitial gaps, and the five structural parameters are fit to the actual square boundary rather than forced into a symmetric lattice. Wall constraint: each row's y is chosen so y−a (or y−b) ≥ 0 and y+a ≤ 1, enforced inside the constructor before SLSQP.
Expected-gain check: with a=0.105, b=0.075 the raw layout already gives 5·3·0.105 + 2·4·0.075 + 2·0.075 = 2.145 from the alternating rows alone plus 2 pocket circles ≈ 2·0.09 → Σr ≈ 2.33 pre-relaxation with substantial SLSQP headroom in the 5 free row parameters; the falsifiable evaluator threshold is Σr > 2.5751 (combined_score > 0.977261), with the incumbent fallback guaranteeing no regression below the current score.

strategies.title: [jammed-polish] Contact-graph freezing + per-circle greedy growth with uniform-s
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: jammed-contact-polish
Replacement scope: replace the 4-iteration "bounded refinement" loop at the end of `construct_packing()` with a two-phase polish: (i) per-circle greedy growth, (ii) brentq uniform rescale.
Compute budget: growth loop ≤ 40 passes, each pass is O(26²) numpy distance checks (no optimizer); brentq with xtol 1e-12, ≤60 function evals; expected +1–2 s, no new SLSQP starts.
Gain mechanism: SLSQP stops at ftol 1e-12 with constraints still having positive slack for many circles (the current output is not jammed). Phase (i): for each circle i compute headroom h_i = min(min-wall-slack, min_j(dist_ij − r_i − r_j)) and grow r_i by h_i − 5e-7 (iterating because growing one circle may shrink another's headroom; accept a pass only if Σr increases, else stop). Phase (ii): after growth, find the exact maximal uniform scale s* via brentq on the max-violation function g(s) = max over pairs/walls of (required − actual distance) for radii s·r, then set r ← (s* − 5e-7/scale)·r. This extracts the residual 1e-3–1e-2 of radius sum SLSQP leaves on the table while the 5e-7 margin keeps every constraint strictly inside the evaluator's 1e-6 tolerance; the incumbent fallback (`best_c, best_r`) is returned unchanged if any intermediate state fails `_feasible` with margin.
Expected-gain check: the incumbent's SLSQP solutions typically carry ≥1e-3 total slack across 26 circles (ftol 1e-12 on a Σr ≈ 2.58 objective leaves per-circle slack ~1e-4–1e-5 each), so the predicted Σr gain is ≈ +2e-3–1e-2, i.e. combined_score ≈ 0.978–0.981 > 0.977261, and the falsifiable threshold is a strict increase of Σr over the incumbent with validity=1 on the evaluator.

strategies.title: [dual-annealing-centers] Stochastic global search over centers with greedy radii
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: dual-annealing-centers
Replacement scope: Replace the seed list and the first-pass SLSQP loop in `construct_packing` with a `scipy.optimize.dual_annealing` stage that optimizes only the 52 center coordinates (radii computed deterministically from centers via the existing greedy-maximal radii routine), followed by one SLSQP polish from the best annealing result.
Compute budget: dual_annealing with maxiter ≤ 300, no separate multistart; plus ≤ 2 SLSQP polish solves (maxiter 400 each). Expected evaluation time ≤ 120 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's SLSQP starts are all trapped in the same hexagonal basin; annealing over centers with a penalized objective −Σ(greedy radii) + λ·(wall/pair violations) can cross basins and find the asymmetric near-optimal arrangement (AlphaEvolve's 2.635 layout is asymmetric). The greedy-radii reduction from 78 to 52 variables removes the flat directions that stall SLSQP. Final SLSQP solve restores exact feasibility; a uniform safety shrink of 2e-7 before return preserves validity against the 1e-6 tolerance.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is basin-hopping over the full center configuration space, which the incumbent's seven hand-designed seeds cannot reach; a falsifiable threshold is any validated sum > 2.5751 (score > 0.97726), with the annealing stage's best-of-run penalized objective directly comparable to the incumbent's 2.5751.

strategies.title: [asymmetric-split] Symmetry-breaking half-split of the incumbent layout with ind
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: asymmetric-split
Replacement scope: Replace the "bounded refinement" perturb-and-resolve loop at the end of `construct_packing` (the 4-iteration RNG perturbation block) with a deterministic symmetry-breaking stage: take the best incumbent centers, mirror-split the square into left/right halves, assign independent radius variables to circles near the mirror axis, and re-solve with SLSQP.
Compute budget: ≤ 3 SLSQP solves (maxiter 400) from the split configurations; no stochastic multistart. Evaluation-time effect ≤ +30 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's best layouts inherit near left-right symmetry, and edge effects mean the true optimum is asymmetric; splitting the mirror-symmetric circles (those with |x−0.5| < 0.15) into independent left/right copies with free radii lets the wall-adjacent side grow larger circles while the interior side shrinks, a degree of freedom the symmetric seeds and perturbations (σ≈0.008) cannot realize. Feasibility is preserved because each SLSQP solve uses the full constraint set and the `_feasible` gate plus a 2e-7 safety shrink before return.
Expected-gain check: the specific new degree of freedom is independent left/right radii on mirror-axis circles, which the incumbent's symmetric seeds cannot express; falsifiable threshold: any validated sum strictly above the incumbent's 2.5750836, checked with the same `_feasible` tolerance.

strategies.title: [corner-anchor] Corner-anchored large-circle lattice with parametric interstitia
strategies.plan:

Replacement scope: Replace `_shell_seed` (the mixed-radius shell layout used as the primary structural seed) with a corner-anchored construction: 4 large corner circles of radius a at (a,a),(1−a,a),(a,1−a),(1−a,1−a); 4 edge-midpoint circles of radius b; and 18 interior circles arranged as 3 staggered hex rows of 6 between the corner circles, with row offsets and radii as free parameters.

strategies.title: [circle-relocation] Smallest-circle eviction and largest-empty-circle reinsertio
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: circle-relocation
Replacement scope: Replace the "Bounded refinement" perturbation loop at the end of `construct_packing` (the 4-iteration jitter-and-resolve block); keep the SLSQP `_run` helper and all seeds as-is.
Compute budget: ≤ 8 relocation rounds; each round evaluates candidate positions (Voronoi vertices + a 9×9 grid, ~100 cheap distance evaluations) and at most one SLSQP re-solve with maxiter 300. Expected total added evaluation time ≤ 60 s on top of the incumbent's ~12 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's refinement only jitters centers by ±0.008, so it can never change the contact topology — a circle that is badly squeezed by its neighbors stays squeezed. This strategy removes the currently smallest-radius circle entirely and reinserts it at the point of maximum clearance from the other 25 circles (found among Voronoi vertices of the remaining centers, clipped into the square, plus a coarse grid fallback), then recomputes greedy-maximal radii for all 26 and polishes with one SLSQP solve. This is a discrete topology move — a new adjacency graph — that continuous perturbation cannot reach; the incumbent's hex-ish layout has several sub-0.08 circles whose radius is set by neighbors on both sides, and relocating one of them into the square's under-used regions (near-wall gaps the hex rows leave at top/bottom) plausibly adds 0.02–0.05 total radius. Validity is preserved by the existing `_feasible` gate plus a final uniform radius shrink of 2e-7 so the 1e-6 evaluator tolerance is never tripped; the incumbent is kept as fallback if no round improves.

strategies.title: [voronoi-lloyd] Power/Voronoi-cell-driven heterogeneous radius assignment
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: voronoi-lloyd
Replacement scope: Replace the seed-generation phase of `construct_packing` (the `seeds` list construction and the `_shell_seed` primary candidate) with a Lloyd-style iteration that produces a heterogeneous-radius seed; keep the SLSQP `_run` solver and feasibility gate unchanged.
Compute budget: ≤ 15 Lloyd iterations (each is one `scipy.spatial.Voronoi` call plus cheap clipping arithmetic), followed by ≤ 4 SLSQP starts with maxiter 400 each; total added time ≤ 40 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's seeds all impose near-equal radii (0.075–0.095 uniform) or one rigid shell parametrization, so SLSQP starts far from the heterogeneous optimum and its gradient steps cannot redistribute radius across the packing. This construction iterates: (1) compute the Voronoi diagram of the 26 centers clipped to the unit square, (2) assign each circle the inradius of its clipped cell (distance to cell walls and to neighboring seeds), (3) move each center toward the incenter of its cell (weighted centroid of the clipped polygon shrunk by the current radius). After ~10 iterations the cells near the square's corners and edges become systematically larger than interior cells, producing a genuinely graded radius field (corner cells ~0.13–0.15, interior ~0.07–0.09) that is a feasible starting point for the existing SLSQP polish. The initial centers come from the existing hex seed, so the fallback incumbent is retained if any iteration produces an infeasible configuration. Validity: radii are always set to the exact inradius minus 1e-7, guaranteeing feasibility before the SLSQP stage, and the final result passes `_feasible` with a 2e-7 uniform safety shrink.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is a spatially graded radius field derived from cell geometry, which neither the uniform-radius seeds nor the 3-parameter shell family can express; falsifiable threshold: sum_radii > 2.5751 on the evaluator.

strategies.title: [perimeter-chain] Wall-tangent spiral chain with inward-shrinking rings
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: perimeter-chain
Replacement scope: Replace `_shell_seed` (and its use as the primary seed in `construct_packing`) with a new parametric perimeter-chain constructor; all other seeds, the SLSQP solver, and the refinement loop stay.
Compute budget: parameter fit via ≤ 6 Nelder-Mead starts with maxiter 300 on ≤ 5 parameters, then ≤ 2 SLSQP starts with maxiter 400; added time ≤ 50 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's families (hex rows, corner anchors, concentric shell rings) all leave systematic dead zones along the square's edges because no circle is forced tangent to the boundary. This construction places every circle tangent to either a wall or two previously placed circles, in a spiral: start with a circle of radius r0 in one corner tangent to both walls; continue placing circles of radius r1 tangent to the bottom wall and the previous circle until the chain reaches the right wall; turn the corner with a radius-r2 circle tangent to both walls; repeat up the right wall, across the top, and down the left wall, then fill the interior with the same tangent-chain rule using decreasing radii r3, r4. The four or five radii parameters (r0…r4) are fitted by Nelder-Mead minimizing the sum of squared gaps (chain-closure residual: the last wall circle must land within tolerance of the first corner circle), which is a small, well-conditioned fit. Because every circle is wall- or double-tangent, the packing is jammed by construction and wastes no space near the boundary — the exact region where the hex and shell layouts lose area. Greedy-maximal radii are then computed for the fitted centers and one SLSQP polish runs. Validity: the chain fit enforces tangency with a 1e-7 gap, greedy radii are feasible by construction, and the final result is gated by `_feasible` plus a 2e-7 uniform shrink, with the incumbent hex fallback retained.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is a boundary-tangent contact topology in which every circle touches a wall or two circles (zero wasted boundary strip), a topology none of the incumbent's interior-seeded families can reach; falsifiable threshold: sum_radii > 2.5751 on the evaluator.

strategies.title:
Mechanism family: jammed-tangency
Replacement scope: Replace the final "circle-r
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: jammed-tangency
Replacement scope: Replace the final "circle-relocation refinement" loop in `construct_packing` (the Voronoi eviction/reinsertion block) with a two-stage jammed-polish: (a) contact-graph freezing + tangency solve, (b) per-circle greedy growth loop.
Compute budget: one `scipy.optimize.root`/`least_squares` solve on ≤ ~60 active touch equations (max 200 iterations), then a growth loop capped at 40 growth rounds, each a single greedy pass (O(n²), no optimizer). Expected total added time < 10 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's SLSQP stops with slack left in the KKT sense: circles that are not jammed retain headroom the joint solver never extracts because its line search stalls on the active constraint set. Stage (a) detects, for the incumbent layout, all pairs (i,j) with gap < 1e-3 and all wall gaps < 1e-3, forms the quadratic system d_ij² = (r_i+r_j)² and wall equations x_i = r_i etc., and solves it with `scipy.optimize.root(method='lm')` holding radii fixed and moving only centers — this converts near-touches into exact touches, freeing space. Stage (b) then repeatedly finds the circle with the largest feasible growth headroom (min over walls and neighbors of (constraint distance − r_i)) and grows it by headroom − 5e-7, re-checking feasibility; this monotonically increases Σr and is exactly the scored quantity. The incumbent lacks any mechanism that grows a single radius after the joint solve; SLSQP's coupled moves cannot realize it. Falsifiable threshold: if the incumbent layout has any circle with headroom > 1e-4 after the joint solve, this stage strictly increases sum_radii; typical headroom across 26 circles after a stalled SLSQP is 1e-3–1e-2 total, predicting sum_radii 2.6115 → ≥ 2.615 (combined_score ≥ 0.9924). Validity is preserved by the internal 5e-7 margin shrink and a final `_feasible` gate before returning.

Mechanism family: asymmetric-dualhex
Replacement scope: Add a new seed generator `_asym_seed()` and insert it as the first entry of the `seeds` list in `construct_packing` (before the shell seeds), so the existing SLSQP `_run` machinery optimizes from it; remove the weakest existing seed (the shifted-hex seed) to keep runtime flat.
Compute budget: one extra SLSQP start, maxiter 400 — same cost as one existing seed; net evaluation time unchanged.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's hex seed is symmetric about the vertical midline, and SLSQP from a symmetric start converges to a symmetric stationary point; published best n=26 packings are asymmetric. The new seed keeps the [4,5,4,5,4,5] staggered-row skeleton but (a) gives the left three columns radius r_L and the right three columns radius r_R with r_L ≠ r_R (start r_L=0.095, r_R=0.080), (b) shifts odd rows' x-offsets by a free parameter δ ∈ [−0.02, 0.02] instead of the fixed 0.1, and (c) drops the 26th circle near a corner rather than at the last row position. This breaks the mirror symmetry the incumbent's seeds all share, opening a different basin whose SLSQP stationary value the current seed set cannot reach — the same solver, a genuinely different escape direction. Validity: the seed is made feasible by the existing `_greedy_radii` shrink before being passed to `_run`, and only accepted through `_feasible`. Falsifiable threshold: if any asymmetric stationary point beats the symmetric one (as edge-effect analysis predicts, since corner circles have larger wall clearance on the diagonal), sum_radii exceeds 2.6115; the accept-only-if-better guard plus incumbent fallback bounds the downside at exactly the incumbent score.

strategies.title:

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: scale-bisection
Replacement scope: Replace the `_shell_seed` internal Nelder–Mead parameter search and its hand-rolled `viol` penalty (which double-counts a `worst_pair` baseline and misclassifies pair-radius needs) with: fixed parametric center templates (the same shell geometry at a fixed (a,b,c)=(0.16,0.08,0.10)) plus a bisection on a single scale factor s applied to all radii, using the existing `_greedy_radii` output as the base radius vector.
Compute budget: ≤ 40 bisection iterations of an O(n²) violation check; removes the 4 Nelder–Mead runs (each 200 iterations) — net evaluation time decreases.
Gain mechanism: For a fixed set of centers, the maximal feasible radius vector is not the greedy pairwise shrink the incumbent uses (which is order-dependent and can leave a circle far smaller than its cell allows); instead solve max s s.t. s·r_greedy is feasible, where feasibility is the exact evaluator predicate (walls + pairwise). Bisection on s with the exact violation function finds the true maximal scaling of that center template, which is ≥ the greedy result by construction (greedy output is one feasible point in the same family). This is a new degree of freedom — the incumbent's greedy shrink never checks whether a globally-scaled version of its radius vector is feasible, and order-dependent shrinking typically loses 1–3% of Σr on mixed-radius templates. Additionally, re-run the bisection for the hex-template centers as a second candidate and keep the better. Validity: the returned radii are feasible by construction of the bisection with a 5e-7 margin, then gated by `_feasible`. Falsifiable threshold: if greedy shrink is suboptimal on either template (checkable in-program: if the bisection's s* > 1 + 1e-4), sum_radii strictly exceeds the incumbent's 2.6115; predicted gain 0.005–0.02 from the shell template alone, giving combined_score ≥ 0.993.
